A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAD neural-network research. Their complete main texts, mathematical statements, figures, references, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original polynomial-fitting, PDE-solving, and MNIST experiments in Section 4, with experimental details and 97.93% MNIST test accuracy in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains original polynomial, PDE, and MNIST results and reports additional full-batch gradient-descent results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The SAD framework, network architecture definition, gradient-flow procedure, and polynomial-approximation construction are retained. The experimental optimizer changes do not introduce a new proposed method or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1D, 2D, and 4D polynomial targets on [-1,1]^d, 10D Heat and Black–Scholes problems, and MNIST classification. The additional gradient-descent panels reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates SGD against Adam for the 1D polynomial, with only Adam shown for 2D and 4D. V2 replaces SGD with full-batch GD and compares it with Adam in all three dimensions. Swish, Softplus, GELU, ELU, and tanh remain the tested activations.

E3.justification: Appendix E changes the gradient-descent branch from SGD batches of 100 at learning rate 0.01 to full-batch GD using all 10,000 training points at 0.001, and extends GD evaluation to 2D and 4D. This substantially changes the optimization regime. Adam settings, network widths, metrics, and practical-task protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 and new Figure 6 add an exploratory growth-rate check: exponentially rescaled parameter-norm axes examine apparent logarithmic growth. This analyzes the rate beyond v1's increasing-norm observation, while reusing the GD trajectories rather than establishing additional runs.

E5.justification: Both versions average polynomial experiments over 20 independent initializations and PDE/MNIST experiments over five. The Monte Carlo reference-solution sampling is also retained. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures appear.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands direct GD validation: Figure 1 replaces the earlier 1D SGD trajectories and adds 2D and 4D GD loss and norm trajectories for five activations. These are results under revised conditions, not same-setting performance gains. The corresponding Adam curves, PDE/MNIST curves, and 97.93% MNIST test accuracy are retained.

T1.justification: The main theorem statements are retained, but v2 corrects the erf normalization, the density formula, and the missing minus sign and square-integrable quantity in Lemma B.2. Corollary A.2 drops the density's definability assumption, and Remark 2.9 restricts its applicability statement to Example 2.4(i)–(xi). These are localized mathematical corrections and refinements.

C1.justification: The claimed contribution is substantially narrowed. V1 presents the dichotomy and polynomial approximation as contributions; v2 explicitly characterizes much of the dichotomy as established and disclaims originality for the approximation proof. Sections 1.1 and 3 instead identify non-representability and the resulting divergence as the central novel contribution, while retaining the principal mathematical conclusions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets GD norm growth as apparently logarithmic and relates its slowness to the retained O(sqrt(t)) bound. It also qualifies the introductory global-minimization framing, restricts the ReLU minimum-existence discussion to shallow networks, and explains degenerate multidimensional datasets in Appendix C. Existing gradient-flow and smoothness limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E revises the sampling and learning-rate specifications, explicitly distinguishing full-batch GD from minibatch Adam. The target formulas, architecture details, Tesla V100 hardware, reported training times, and code/test-plot access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands approximation and optimization literature, including Cybenko, Hornik and colleagues, De Ryck and colleagues, DeVore and colleagues, and Pinkus. Sections 1.1–1.2 and Appendices B–D explicitly connect the dichotomy and approximation results to prior work, materially repositioning novelty around non-representability.

P1.justification: The section sequence and Appendices A–E remain intact. Focused rewrites affect the contribution discussion, Section 4.1, and proof overviews in Appendices B–D. V2 also standardizes derivative terminology and expands the author affiliations and publication header.

P2.justification: The polynomial-results presentation is substantially rebuilt: v1's mixed four-column Figure 1 becomes separate three-column GD and Adam Figures 1–2. V2 adds the rescaled Figure 6 and enlarges the retained PDE/MNIST display as Figure 3. The two appendix proof diagrams are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision through clearer attribution of established results, localized mathematical corrections, and more accessible proof explanations. Full-batch GD across all polynomial dimensions also better connects the numerical evidence to gradient flow, although it replaces the earlier SGD evidence and does not establish same-setting gains. The main theorems and practical-task results remain largely unchanged, making the overall improvement limited.
